name: builds-core-frosted-toolbar-without-package
prompt: Implement a frosted floating action toolbar in an existing Flutter app using its current theme. The requested effect is blur, tint, and a fine edge highlight over changing content; no refraction, shader, or new package is requested. Explain why the backdrop should use BackdropFilter rather than filtering only the toolbar child, and describe the verification approach without claiming unavailable renders.
expectations: uses a tightly clipped BackdropFilter layer with tint and edge treatment and distinguishes backdrop sampling from filtering one child
reuses the existing theme and avoids adding an effect package or competing component system
places decorative effect layers behind semantics and hit testing and limits interactive feedback to actual controls
specifies comparable busy-background, light, dark, high-contrast, and opaque-fallback verification without fabricating rendered evidence

name: translates-ios-liquid-glass-with-fidelity-ladder
prompt: Translate a supplied iOS 26 SwiftUI floating tool palette into Flutter for iOS, Android, and web. The reference uses GlassEffectContainer, glassEffect, glassProminent, interactive highlights, and a matched morph between collapsed and expanded controls. Preserve its visual intent, accessibility alternatives, and interaction semantics without claiming exact Apple material parity or unavailable device results.
expectations: extracts blur, tint, edge light, refraction, grouping, prominence, and morphing as separate transferable properties instead of copying SwiftUI API names
defines a fidelity ladder from opaque fallback through core material to shader or native rendering and chooses per supported target
keeps timing and shared-geometry choreography separate from optical rendering while preserving stable identity
defines reduced-transparency, reduced-motion, contrast, unsupported-renderer, screenshot, and profile-mode verification without claiming exact native parity

name: gates-experimental-liquid-renderer
prompt: A Flutter team wants refractive liquid-glass controls on Android, iOS, and web and suggests adding liquid_glass_renderer immediately. No repository or hardware results are supplied. Provide a production decision and implementation plan using current project evidence when available; do not invent package support or performance results.
expectations: requires inspecting pubspec, current package metadata, SDK, platform and renderer support, maintenance, license, and documented limitations before adoption

expectations.text: does not treat an experimental effect renderer as a universal dependency or claim unsupported web and device behavior

expectations: defines core or opaque fallbacks before integration and preserves layout and interaction semantics across fidelity tiers
requires profile-mode scrolling and interaction evidence on representative hardware plus first-use shader or texture checks before default enablement

name: reuses-existing-effect-package
prompt: An existing Flutter app already depends on a maintained visual-effects package and uses its GlassSurface and ReducedTransparencyFallback widgets in production on iOS and Android. Extend the current floating toolbar to use the same material family; first inspect the package entry, source usage, theme contract, targets, and fallback. Provide a concrete before/after fixture matrix and separate planned checks from observed evidence; do not migrate packages or claim unavailable renders.
expectations: inspects and reuses the existing package, widgets, theme contract, and fallback instead of hand-rolling a parallel renderer
checks the current implementation and project constraints before deciding whether any package change is necessary
keeps interaction semantics, accessibility fallback, and platform behavior consistent with the existing effect system

expectations.text: defines a before-and-after fixture comparison and reports only rendered or profiled evidence that actually exists

name: chooses-package-for-common-complex-effect
prompt: A Flutter product needs a production-grade particle burst and grouped liquid surfaces. A maintained package claims support for the project's Android, iOS, and web targets, while a custom shader would take several weeks. Explain how to decide between the package and custom implementation before coding; no repository, package audit, or device profile is supplied.
expectations: treats a maintained package as a serious candidate for a complex common capability rather than assuming custom code is superior
requires current package, SDK, renderer, platform, license, maintenance, fallback, and performance checks before adoption
keeps custom shader as the alternative when the package fails fidelity, platform, or control requirements and compares total maintenance risk
defines a small prototype and profile-mode evidence matrix before making the package or custom path the default
